Greek and Latin Languages and Cultures

Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam

← Back to search
About this programme

UCR currently cannot construct a sufficiently close programme for a meaningful curriculum comparison.

VU Greek and Latin Languages and Cultures combines advanced reading and interpretation of Greek and Latin texts with linguistics, literature, ancient cultural history, philosophy and the later reception of antiquity. Students progress from language and textual foundations to specialist study and independent classical research.

UCR offers valuable study of ancient myth, Greek archaeology and democratic heritage, rhetoric, philosophy and literary interpretation. These contributions do not form a complete programme centred on the sustained philological study of Greek and Latin texts, their linguistic structures and their transmission. We therefore show the verified VU curriculum without presenting a UCR programme as a comparable alternative.

Academic year: 2026–2027

External pathway: Standard bachelor; no formal specialisation

The 180 EC pathway comprises 60 EC of first-year study, 78 EC of later compulsory courses, a 12 EC thesis including colloquium and 30 EC of open study. Comedy is an optional additional module. Thesis entry requires all first- and second-year courses. The Dutch diagnostic or remedial language requirement adds no credits; specified practical courses require 85% attendance.
